backend: headless Chromium, production platform module and real WASM worker

checks.action: Diagnostic boot, focus 3D canvas, hold/release Digit1
Orbit to top; hover and physically click/hold/release visible middle pad
Load official V1.5.1 local image; click Skip on real 2D display
Open an independent mini share with pinned first-party diagnostic manifest, restore product/mappings, press/release back pad
Embed share in same-origin iframe; source/origin/session-bound hello and call RPC; press/release middle pad
Abort K151 model.json request; load diagnostic and physically press panel front-pad button
Fresh page load with final source and adequate local HTTP accept queue; inspect hover hit classes

reproduction: Build examples/platform-stackchan as documented, then tools/wasm-build.sh; serve web/ locally with concurrent module requests supported.
Use window.espTester.configure with createDefaultScene(catalog, "m5stack-k151"), then load the diagnostic local build and start.
Hold the three pad IDs through keyboard/3D or API; verify fresh guest serial, RGB, positionDegrees and the actual framebuffer.

For sharing, serve the first-party build with a pinned manifest and artifact SHA-256 values; share({mode:"embed",autostart:false,includeRecording:false}). Load/start through the same API in mini and the documented parent RPC.
For fallback, intercept only assets/m5stack-k151/model.json; verify the 2D view and real panel input still work.
limitations: No physical hardware comparison; diagnostic actions do not certify all factory apps.
Raw images are retained locally outside Git; no public capture archive is claimed.
Initial test harness used a low-backlog static HTTP server, which intermittently reset module requests; fresh-page check used a larger accept queue.
An iframe load event can precede asynchronous application initialization; hello must be retried or sent once the app is ready.
Top pad boundaries, spatial LED order and joint zero/direction remain uncalibrated.
